doc.title: System Architecture - OpenAI Analysis Layer
doc.snippet: The OpenAI Analysis Layer sends structured data to OpenAI and gets probability estimates. Modules include prompt_builder.py (constructs analysis prompt), client.py (manages API calls), response_parser.py (parses output). Prompt strategy: Input JSON with fixture, form, injuries, odds → Output JSON with markets array, probabilities, reasoning.

doc.title: Story 4.1: Build OpenAI Prompt Builder
doc.snippet: Story definition from development roadmap. Create /src/bet_bot/analysis/ai/prompt_builder.py module. Build prompt including fixture details, team form, injury info, H2H history, current odds. Format data clearly for AI understanding. Request probabilities for match result, total goals, corners, cards. Request reasoning explanation. Keep prompt concise (less than 2000 tokens).

doc.title: Data Schema and Field Definitions
doc.snippet: Fixture model contains: id (str), home_team (Team), away_team (Team), league (str), kickoff_time (datetime), odds (dict[str, dict[str, float]]), head_to_head_history (list). Team model contains: id (str), name (str), form_5_games (list[str]), avg_goals_for (float), avg_goals_against (float), injuries (list).

doc.title: Data Quality Scoring (Story 3.3)
doc.snippet: Each fixture has quality_score (0-100) attached from Story 3.3. Quality score informs prompt confidence and helps decide which data to emphasize. Fixtures from Story 3.3 are already validated and consolidated before reaching prompt builder.

artifact.reason: Core Fixture model that the prompt builder receives as input. Defines Team, League, and Fixture Pydantic models with validation. Story 4.1 uses Fixture objects populated by Story 3.3 consolidation pipeline.
AIAnalysis and MarketAnalysis models define the expected output format from OpenAI. Story 4.2 will parse OpenAI responses into this format. Story 4.1 prompt should request JSON matching this schema.
Form data models used to represent team recent performance. Story 4.1 accesses form_5_games from Team model to build team form section of prompt.
Injury models define injured player information structure. Story 4.1 formats injury data from Team.injuries list into human-readable prompt section.
Odds models define odds data structure. Story 4.1 accesses Fixture.odds dict to extract market probabilities and formats them for prompt.
Quality scoring from Story 3.3 attaches quality_score to each fixture (0-100). Story 4.1 uses quality_score to decide which data to emphasize and inform prompt confidence level.

Validation from Story 3.2 checks data freshness. Story 4.1 receives fixtures already validated for freshness and can focus on fixture-specific data validation (non-null fields, kickoff time not in past).
Logging utility from Story 1.5. Story 4.1 must follow existing logging patterns: DEBUG for raw prompts, INFO for fixture summaries, WARNING for validation failures.

constraint.description: Must use Python 3.14+ compatible syntax. NO datetime.utcnow() - use datetime.now(timezone.utc). Use modern type hints: list[X], dict[K,V], X | None instead of List, Dict, Optional. All functions must have explicit return type annotations including -> None.

Main function build_analysis_prompt() must be marked async for consistency with Story 4.4 orchestration. Use asyncio patterns if parallel operations needed, but current story is pure formatting (no blocking I/O).

Follow CLAUDE.md error handling patterns: Use custom exception hierarchy (not generic Exception). Log all validation failures at WARNING level. Graceful degradation: If data missing, continue without it (don't fail). Never swallow exceptions without logging.
Must use Pydantic v2 syntax. Use @field_validator (not @validator). Use ConfigDict (not Config class). All models require populate_by_name=True if aliases used.

Implement _validate_fixture_for_prompt() that checks: fixture_id exists and non-empty, home_team and away_team with ids/names, league name exists, kickoff_time is datetime and not in past, odds dict is non-empty with at least match_result market. Log validation failures at WARNING, return True/False.

Estimate token count before sending. Use conservative estimate: tokens ≈ words / 0.75. Warn at 1800 tokens, error/reject at 2500 tokens. Include system prompt, fixture, and request tokens in estimate.

Prompt must be human-readable (for debugging) AND include structured JSON request format. Specify expected JSON response format in prompt with example. Response schema must match AIAnalysis model from Story 2.1.
Prompt must be less than 2000 tokens total. Request concise reasoning (max 100 words per market). Include quality_score assessment to justify data confidence level.

DEBUG: raw prompt (first 500 chars for sampling). INFO: fixture summary (teams, league, market count), estimated token count. WARNING: validation failures, data issues, token count approaching 1800. NEVER log API keys or sensitive data. Include fixture_id in all messages.

Create /src/bet_bot/analysis/ai/__init__.py (if not exists). Main entry point: build_analysis_prompt() function (async). Helper functions: _validate_fixture_for_prompt(), _format_fixture_details(), _format_team_form(), _format_injuries(), _format_h2h_history(), _format_odds(), _format_analysis_request(), _estimate_token_count(), _get_available_markets(). Integration function: export_prompt_for_api().

export_prompt_for_api() function should return dict with keys: "system_prompt" (str), "user_message" (str). System prompt defines AI as sports betting analyst. This format is ready for OpenAI client integration in Story 4.2.

interface.name: build_analysis_prompt()
interface.description: Main entry point. Validates fixture, builds all data sections, assembles prompt with system instructions, enforces token limit, returns complete prompt string ready for OpenAI API.
interface.input: Fixture object from Story 3.3 (consolidated and scored)
interface.output: String containing complete prompt (system + user message parts)

interface.name: export_prompt_for_api()
interface.description: Integration helper for Story 4.2. Wraps build_analysis_prompt() output into dict format for OpenAI client.

interface.name: _validate_fixture_for_prompt()
interface.description: Validates fixture has all required fields for prompt building. Logs at WARNING if validation fails. Returns True/False (raises exception only on critical failures).

interface.name: Fixture model interface
interface.description: Input data structure from Story 3.3 consolidation. Contains all fields needed: fixture_id, kickoff_time, home_team (with form_5_games, injuries), away_team, league, odds dict (market → outcome → odds), head_to_head_history list.
interface.fields: fixture_id: str kickoff_time: datetime (timezone-aware) home_team: Team (with id, name, form_5_games, avg_goals_for, avg_goals_against, injuries) away_team: Team league: League (league_id, league_name, league_country, league_season) odds: dict[str, dict[str, float]] (e.g., {"match_result": {"home": 2.1, "draw": 3.5, "away": 3.2}}) head_to_head_history: list[str] (W/D/L from home perspective)

interface.name: AIAnalysis response schema
interface.description: Expected OpenAI response format that prompt should request. Contains fixture_id, markets array with MarketAnalysis objects (market_type, ai_probability, reasoning, confidence), analysis_timestamp.
interface.fields: fixture_id: str markets: list[MarketAnalysis] analysis_timestamp: datetime Each market: type, probabilities (dict), reasoning (str)

interface.name: Logging patterns
interface.description: Existing logging setup from Story 1.5. Use logger.debug(), logger.info(), logger.warning() following established patterns. Never log API keys. Include fixture_id for traceability.

tests.standards: Testing framework: pytest (with pytest-asyncio for async tests). Model validation: pytest fixtures for sample data, use Pydantic validators. Coverage target: 85%+ code coverage for prompt_builder.py. Pattern: Arrange-Act-Assert (AAA) structure. Mock data using sample fixtures from development-stories.md. Test async functions with @pytest.mark.asyncio decorator.
tests.locations: /tests/unit/test_prompt_builder.py - Main test file /tests/unit/test_models.py - Existing model validation tests (already covering Fixture, Team, League) /tests/fixtures/ - Sample data (if needed for test fixtures)
tests.ideas: Test fixture validation: Valid fixture passes, missing fixture_id fails, missing teams fails, teams without ids fail, past kickoff_time fails, empty odds fails. Test fixture details formatter: Correct format with all fields, handles missing location, cleans team names (whitespace, HTML). Test team form formatter: Includes recent form and win %, handles missing form data, calculates win % correctly (W=1, D=0.5, L=0). Test injury formatter: Lists injuries with positions, handles no injuries, limits to 5 players max. Test H2H formatter: Shows last 5 matches correctly, calculates H2H record, handles no H2H data. Test odds formatter: Shows all available markets, calculates implied probabilities, handles missing markets gracefully. Test analysis request formatter: Requests all four markets (match_result, total_goals, corners, cards), requests reasoning, specifies JSON format. Test prompt assembly: Validates before assembling, includes all sections in order, no duplication. Test token counting: Estimates within 10% of actual for typical fixtures, warns on high token count, raises on > 2500 tokens. Test edge cases: Minimal data (only required fields), all optional data, long team names (50+ chars), Unicode characters, old H2H data (20+ matches), missing optional fields.
